excerpt: Rec Room was a free social VR and cross-platform game where players built and shared rooms. It shut down on 1 June 2026; Snap acquired selected assets.
content:
Rec Room was a free-to-play social game and creation platform, playable in virtual reality headsets and on ordinary screens. Players met in shared rooms, played mini-games such as paintball and quests, and built their own rooms and games with in-game tools, earning money through a token economy. It was one of the best-known social VR platforms and, the company said, reached more than 150 million players and creators over its life.

Rec Room was founded in 2016. At its peak it was richly funded: PocketGamer.biz reported a $145 million round at a $3.5 billion valuation. Growth did not turn into profit. After laying off roughly half its staff, the company announced in March 2026 that it would close, saying it had never worked out how to make Rec Room a sustainably profitable business because costs always overwhelmed revenue. Token purchases stopped on 1 May 2026, creators stopped earning token rewards after 18 May, and all servers, the rec.net website and the Rec Room Studio tools went offline at noon Pacific time on 1 June 2026. Road to VR, citing GeekWire, reported that Snap acquired selected assets and that some staff joined Specs Inc., Snap's subsidiary working on augmented reality glasses.

Rec Room can no longer be played or bought, and its website now shows only a holding page, so there is nothing to price. This page is kept as a record of what the platform was. Players who want something similar can look at VRChat, Roblox or Horizon Worlds, which offer comparable social spaces and creator tools.

We have not used Rec Room for this page. It brings together Rec Room's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from. Nothing here is paid placement.
